name: progress-claim
title: Progress claim
for_each: select c.claim_id as id, (c.ref || ' ' || c.job) as name from v_claims c order by c.claimed_on desc

sections.title: The claim
sections.note: A payment claim under the Construction Contracts Act 2002. It states the amount, what it is for, and when it is due; the payer responds with payment or a payment schedule.
sections.sql: select c.ref as claim, c.job_ref as job, c.job as for_the_job, c.client as to_the_client, to_char(c.claimed_on, 'DD Month YYYY') as claimed, to_char(c.amount, 'FM$999,999,990') as amount_claimed, case when c.retention_held > 0 then to_char(c.retention_held, 'FM$999,999,990') else 'none' end as retention_held, to_char(c.due_on, 'DD Month YYYY') as payment_due, c.state from v_claims c where c.claim_id = $1

sections.title: The position on this contract
sections.note: Total claims never pass the contract value plus approved variations.
sections.sql: select to_char(j.contract_value, 'FM$999,999,990') as contract_value, case when j.approved_variations > 0 then to_char(j.approved_variations, 'FM$999,999,990') else 'none' end as approved_variations, to_char(j.revised_contract, 'FM$999,999,990') as revised_contract, to_char(j.claimed, 'FM$999,999,990') as claimed_to_date, to_char(j.paid, 'FM$999,999,990') as paid_to_date from v_jobs j join v_claims c on c.job_ref = j.ref where c.claim_id = $1

sections.title: Approved variations on this job
sections.sql: select v.ref, v.description, to_char(v.price, 'FM$999,999,990') as price, to_char(v.decided_on, 'YYYY-MM-DD') as approved_on, v.approved_by from v_variations v join v_claims c on c.job_ref = v.job_ref where c.claim_id = $1 and v.status = 'approved' order by v.decided_on

name: variation-letter
title: Variation for approval
for_each: select v.variation_id as id, (v.ref || ' ' || v.job) as name from v_variations v order by v.proposed_on desc

sections.title: The variation
sections.note: No variation work starts, and none is claimable, until this is approved in writing.
sections.sql: select v.ref, v.job_ref as job, v.job as for_the_job, v.client as to_the_client, v.description, to_char(v.price, 'FM$999,999,990') as price, to_char(v.proposed_on, 'DD Month YYYY') as proposed, v.status, coalesce(v.approved_by, 'awaiting written approval') as approved_by from v_variations v where v.variation_id = $1

sections.title: What it does to the contract
sections.sql: select to_char(j.contract_value, 'FM$999,999,990') as contract_value, to_char(j.approved_variations, 'FM$999,999,990') as variations_approved_so_far, to_char(j.revised_contract + case when v.status = 'proposed' then v.price else 0 end, 'FM$999,999,990') as contract_if_approved from v_jobs j join v_variations v on v.job_ref = j.ref where v.variation_id = $1

name: job-cost-report
title: Job cost report
for_each: select j.job_id as id, (j.ref || ' ' || j.job) as name from v_jobs j where j.status in ('active', 'complete') order by j.ref

sections.title: The job
sections.sql: select j.ref, j.job, j.client, coalesce(j.site_address, '') as site, j.job_type as type, j.status, to_char(j.revised_contract, 'FM$999,999,990') as contract, to_char(j.claimed, 'FM$999,999,990') as claimed, to_char(j.costs_actual, 'FM$999,999,990') as costs_to_date, case when j.committed > 0 then to_char(j.committed, 'FM$999,999,990') else 'none' end as committed, to_char(j.forecast_margin, 'FM$999,999,990') as forecast_margin from v_jobs j where j.job_id = $1

sections.title: Budget vs actual, line by line
sections.note: Committed is open purchase orders. A line marked OVER is a conversation this week, not a surprise in the final account.
sections.sql: select b.cost_code as code, b.line, to_char(b.budget, 'FM$999,999,990') as budget, to_char(b.actual, 'FM$999,999,990') as actual, case when b.committed > 0 then to_char(b.committed, 'FM$999,999,990') else '' end as committed, to_char(b.remaining, 'FM$999,999,990') as remaining, b.state from v_budget b where b.job_id = $1 order by b.cost_code

sections.title: Variations
sections.sql: select v.ref, v.description, to_char(v.price, 'FM$999,999,990') as price, v.status, coalesce(v.approved_by, '') as approved_by from v_variations v join v_jobs j on j.ref = v.job_ref where j.job_id = $1 order by v.proposed_on

sections.title: Progress claims
sections.sql: select c.ref, to_char(c.claimed_on, 'YYYY-MM-DD') as claimed, to_char(c.amount, 'FM$999,999,990') as amount, to_char(c.due_on, 'YYYY-MM-DD') as due, coalesce(to_char(c.paid_on, 'YYYY-MM-DD'), '') as paid, c.state from v_claims c join v_jobs j on j.ref = c.job_ref where j.job_id = $1 order by c.claimed_on
